questions.q: What was the Mole doing at the very start of the chapter?
choices: Spring-cleaning his little home
Digging a new tunnel to the river
Packing a picnic basket
Sleeping through the winter

questions.q: Why did the Mole suddenly throw down his brush and leave the house?
choices: Spring was calling him and he was tired of cleaning
He heard the Rat calling him from the river
His house had flooded
He had run out of whitewash
questions.evidence: 'Hang spring-cleaning!' and bolted out of the house

questions.q: What did the elderly rabbit at the gap in the hedge ask the Mole for?
choices: Sixpence to pass along the private road
Directions to the river
Some food to share
His name and address
questions.evidence: Sixpence for the privilege of passing by the private road!

questions.q: The Mole was "bewitched, entranced, fascinated" by the river. What does "entranced" mean here?
choices: Filled with wonder and delight
Frightened and nervous
Bored and sleepy
Confused and lost
questions.evidence: The Mole was bewitched, entranced, fascinated.

questions.q: What first caught the Mole's eye in the dark hole across the river?
choices: Something small and bright that twinkled, which turned out to be an eye
A lantern hanging in the doorway
A fish jumping out of the water
A glow-worm resting on a leaf
questions.evidence: it winked at him, and so declared itself to be an eye

questions.q: How did the Rat bring the Mole across the river?
choices: In a little blue-and-white boat
On his back while swimming
Over a wooden bridge
On a raft made of reeds
questions.evidence: It was painted blue outside and white within

questions.q: According to the Rat, what is the thing most worth doing in the whole world?
choices: Simply messing about in boats
Reading poetry by the fire
Exploring the Wide World
Having picnics with friends
questions.evidence: half so much worth doing as simply messing about in boats

questions.q: What happened while the Rat was dreamily talking about messing about in boats?
choices: The boat struck the bank and the Rat fell over backwards
The Otter popped up beside the boat
The Mole fell into the water
A storm began to blow
questions.evidence: The boat struck the bank full tilt.

questions.q: What did the Rat bring out of his house before the two set off down the river?
choices: A fat wicker luncheon-basket
A fishing rod and net
A map of the river
A warm coat for the Mole
questions.evidence: staggering under a fat, wicker luncheon-basket

questions.q: How did the Rat answer when the Mole asked whether life by the river was dull?
choices: He said the bank was so crowded with busy animals that it was never dull
He admitted it was very lonely
He said he only had the river to talk to
He said he was planning to move away
questions.evidence: The bank is so crowded nowadays that many people are moving away altogether

questions.q: From the way the Rat talks about the Wild Wood, what can you tell about it?
choices: It can be dangerous, because some of its animals cannot be trusted
It is the Rat's favorite place to visit
Nobody at all lives there
It is where the Rat grew up
questions.evidence: you can't really trust them, and that's the fact

questions.q: What did the Rat tell the Mole about the Wide World beyond the Wild Wood?
choices: He had never been there and never meant to go
He traveled there every summer
It was full of friendly rabbits
It was where Badger lived
questions.evidence: I've never been there, and I'm never going

questions.q: What did the Badger do when the Rat called to him at the picnic?
choices: He grunted 'Company,' turned his back and left
He sat down and joined them for lunch
He scolded the Mole for being there
He invited them all to his house
questions.evidence: 'H'm! Company,' and turned his back and disappeared from view.

questions.q: What do the Rat and the Otter say Toad is like?
choices: He takes up a new hobby, gets tired of it, and starts something fresh
He is shy and never leaves his house
He is the best rower on the river
He is mean and unkind to everyone
questions.evidence: he gets tired of it, and starts on something fresh

questions.q: The Rat calls the picnic "an impromptu affair." What does "impromptu" mean?
choices: Not planned ahead of time
Very fancy and expensive
Secret and private
Long and boring

questions.q: What happened right after the Mole grabbed the sculls and tried to row?
choices: The boat tipped over and he fell into the river
He rowed them safely home
The Rat let him row the rest of the way
They crashed into Toad's wager-boat
questions.evidence: Over went the boat, and he found himself struggling in the river.

questions.q: How did the Rat respond after the Mole apologized for upsetting the boat?
choices: He forgave him and invited him to stay and learn to row and swim
He sent the Mole home angrily
He said the Mole could never ride in his boat again
He made the Mole pay for the lost basket
questions.evidence: I really think you had better come and stop with me for a little time

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: The Mole discovers the river and begins a new friendship with the Rat
The Mole and the Rat get lost in the Wild Wood
Toad wins a boat race on the river
The Badger teaches the Mole to swim
questions.evidence: This day was only the first of many similar ones for the emancipated Mole
